## 1. Goal

Run E5 (when does reservation pay off?) across shares of big-memory jobs, aging vs reserve, and write `e5_summary.csv` in the PRD §5 format.

## 2. Background

**From BLUEPRINT §6 E5:**

| # | Question | What we vary | Graph |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E5 | When does reservation pay off? | Share of big-memory jobs (0% to 40%) | Maximum wait with and without reservation |

**From PRD §5 Summary CSV formats (e5 row):**

| File | Rows (key) | `setting` / `x_value` | `policy` values | Metric columns (each with `_mean`, `_ci_low`, `_ci_high`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `e5_summary.csv` | (E5, big-memory share, policy) | `setting` = `big_mem_pct=<v>`; `x_value` = share of big-memory jobs in percent, 0–40 | `aging`, `reserve` | `max_wait`, `avg_wait` |

## 9. How to verify

```sh
python tools/run_experiments.py --experiment E5 && python tools/summarize.py --experiments E5 && pytest tests/py/test_summaries.py -q
```

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** more big-memory jobs → more resource starvation under aging alone → reservation should cut the maximum wait.
**Examiner question:** "When does reservation not help?" — With no big jobs; then it rarely triggers and both curves match.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Different workloads for aging and reserve (must be the same seeds)
